images.title: One half in eighths
images.purpose: Show that one half of a chikki is the same as 4 eighths, so it can be counted against 5 eighths in the same unit.
images.composition: Two long chikki bars stacked with wide space between them, left edges aligned, and one comparison line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Top: one flat rectangular chikki bar cut into 8 equal pieces by thin lines, with one thicker line at the exact middle; the left 4 pieces filled teal #0072B2, the right 4 plain. Below it: one chikki bar of exactly the same length, left edges aligned, cut into 8 equal pieces; the left 5 pieces filled amber #E69F00, the right 3 plain. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 outline around the 5th amber piece, the one extra eighth. Centred below both bars: one comparison line. Exactly 2 bars, 16 pieces, 4 teal, 5 amber.

images.takeaway: Count both shares in eighths, then compare: 4 eighths is less than 5 eighths.
images.description: Two same-length chikki bars cut into 8 equal pieces: 4 teal pieces show 1/2 = 4/8 and 5 amber pieces show 5/8, with the extra eighth outlined, so 4/8 < 5/8.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the middle line of the top bar and count the teal eighths in that half.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the half as 4 eighths next to 5 eighths is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
